cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does MongoDB handle database creation when you run the `use <databaseName>` command?
cards.back: Running `use schoolDB` selects the database in memory; disk creation happens on first insert.
cards.key_takeaway: MongoDB creates a database on disk lazily only after the first document is inserted.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
mindmap
  root(("Lazy Database Creation"))
    "use schoolDB selects in memory"
    "No dedicated create command"
    "Created on first insert"
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: Which shell command lists all materialized databases on the connected MongoDB server along with their disk size?
cards.back: Running `show dbs` prints populated databases such as `admin 0.000GB`, `config 0.000GB`, `local 0.000GB`, and `schoolDB 0.000GB`.
cards.key_takeaway: The show dbs command enumerates only databases that physically hold data on disk.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Run show dbs"] --> B["Query Storage Catalog"]
    B["Query Storage Catalog"] --> C["Print Populated DBs and Sizes"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle > Database Catalog Inspection (show dbs)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: True or False — Running `use schoolDB` immediately creates `schoolDB` on disk so it appears in `show dbs`? Explain why.
cards.back: **False.** Running `use schoolDB` only switches the session pointer in memory; `schoolDB` remains hidden from `show dbs` until a document is written.
cards.key_takeaway: Unwritten databases selected with use remain invisible in show dbs until data is inserted.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    W["❌ Misconception: use schoolDB creates DB on disk immediately"] --> R["✅ Reality: DB is created and listed in show dbs only after first write"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle > Database Context Switching & Creation (use <databaseName>)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In the database decommissioning workflow, what happens when `db.dropDatabase()` executes after `use schoolDB`?
cards.back: Always verify your active database context before running `db.dropDatabase()` because it irreversibly removes every collection and document inside it.
cards.key_takeaway: Executing db.dropDatabase permanently and irreversibly deletes the active database and all its contents.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Step 1: Select Context via use schoolDB"] --> B["Step 2: Execute db.dropDatabase()"]
    B["Step 2: Execute db.dropDatabase()"] --> C["Step 3: Database and Collections Permanently Removed"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 1. Database Operations & Storage Lifecycle > Database Destruction & Removal (db.dropDatabase())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does implicit collection auto-creation differ from explicit `db.createCollection()` in terms of setup timing and options?
cards.back: Implicit creation happens automatically on first insert, whereas explicit creation pre-configures validation rules or capped sizes.
cards.key_takeaway: Collections are created either automatically upon first document insert or explicitly via db.createCollection.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Collection Provisioning Mode"] --> A["Implicit: Auto-created on first insert"]
    D["Collection Provisioning Mode"] --> B["Explicit: db.createCollection with options"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 2. Collection Architecture & Structural Management

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: What is the function of the `show collections` command in the MongoDB shell?
cards.back: For example, inside `schoolDB`, running `show collections` displays `students`.
cards.key_takeaway: The show collections command lists all materialized collections in the active database.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
mindmap
  root(("show collections"))
    "Scoped to active database"
    "Lists materialized collections"
    "Requires explicit create or first insert"
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 2. Collection Architecture & Structural Management > Collection Inventory Inspection (show collections)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In the Collection Removal Mechanics diagram, what components are destroyed when `db.students.drop()` is executed?
cards.back: Executing `db.students.drop()` permanently removes the `students` collection container, all stored documents, and all indexes.
cards.key_takeaway: Dropping a collection permanently removes its container, all documents, and all associated indexes.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["db.students.drop() Execution"] --> B["Destroy Collection Container"]
    A["db.students.drop() Execution"] --> C["Purge All Documents and Indexes"]
```

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does `insertOne()` differ from `insertMany()` in terms of the argument structure passed to the method?
cards.back:
- `insertMany([doc1, doc2, ...])` inserts multiple documents in a single call, passed as an array."

`insertOne()` accepts one document object `{...}`, while `insertMany()` requires an array `[{...}, {...}]`.
cards.key_takeaway: Use insertOne for a single document object and insertMany for an array of multiple documents.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Input Payload Structure"] --> A["insertOne: Single Document Object {...}"]
    D["Input Payload Structure"] --> B["insertMany: Array of Documents [{...}, {...}]"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 3. Document Ingestion Mechanics (CRUD Create)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does `find()` differ from `findOne()` in terms of the return value produced by the query?
cards.back:
- `findOne(query, projection)` retrieves just the first matching document (or null), instead of a cursor."

`find()` streams matches via a cursor; `findOne()` returns one document or `null`.
cards.key_takeaway: The find method returns a cursor over all matches, while findOne returns only the first matching document or null.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Query Return Value"] --> A["find(): Iterable Cursor over all matches"]
    D["Query Return Value"] --> B["findOne(): First matched document or null"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 4. Document Retrieval & Query Architecture (CRUD Read)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: What does calling `db.students.find()` with no arguments or an empty filter `{}` return?
cards.back: Both `db.students.find()` and `db.students.find({})` match and return a cursor over every document in `students`.
cards.key_takeaway: An empty filter object or omitted filter in find matches every document in the collection.
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 4. Document Retrieval & Query Architecture (CRUD Read) > Cursor-Based Querying (find())

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: What overall architectural concept does the Advanced Query Filtering, Projection, and Pagination diagram illustrate?
cards.back: It illustrates how MongoDB chains predicate filtering, field projection, and `sort().skip().limit()` pagination.
cards.key_takeaway: MongoDB read queries combine row-level filtering, column-level projection, and cursor-level sort/skip/limit modifiers.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["find(query, projection) Pipeline"] --> B["1. Filter Matching Documents"]
    A["find(query, projection) Pipeline"] --> C["2. Project Included/Excluded Fields"]
    A["find(query, projection) Pipeline"] --> D["3. Chain sort, skip, and limit"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 5. Advanced Query Filtering, Projection & Pagination

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In the cursor ordering parameter table, what do the numeric values `1` and `-1` represent inside `sort({ field: 1 | -1 })`?
cards.back: Passing `db.students.find().sort({ age: 1 })` sorts ages lowest to highest, whereas `db.students.find().sort({ age: -1 })` sorts ages highest to lowest.
cards.key_takeaway: In sort, 1 orders results in ascending order and -1 orders results in descending order.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["sort({ field: 1 | -1 })"] --> B["Value 1 -> Ascending (Lowest to Highest)"]
    A["sort({ field: 1 | -1 })"] --> C["Value -1 -> Descending (Highest to Lowest)"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 5. Advanced Query Filtering, Projection & Pagination > Cursor Pipeline Transformation & Pagination

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does `updateOne(filter, update)` differ from `updateMany(filter, update)` in terms of document mutation scope?
cards.back:
- `updateMany(filter, update)` applies the same update to every matching document."

`updateOne()` modifies only the first match, while `updateMany()` modifies all matching documents.
cards.key_takeaway: Use updateOne to modify the first matching document and updateMany to modify all matching documents.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Update Mutation Scope"] --> A["updateOne: Modifies first matching document"]
    D["Update Mutation Scope"] --> B["updateMany: Modifies every matching document"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 6. Field Modification & In-Place Update Operators (CRUD Update)

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: In the Update Operators reference table, what action does each of the four operators (`$set`, `$inc`, `$push`, `$pull`) perform?
cards.back: `$set` updates a field, `$inc` increments a number, `$push` appends to an array, and `$pull` removes matching items from an array.
cards.key_takeaway: MongoDB provides $set and $inc for scalar fields, and $push and $pull for array fields.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Scalar Operators"] --> B["$set: Replace Value | $inc: Increment Number"]
    C["Array Operators"] --> D["$push: Add to Array | $pull: Remove from Array"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 6. Field Modification & In-Place Update Operators (CRUD Update) > Atomic Field Update Operators

cards.chapter: VVIT MongoDB: Databases, Collections & CRUD Operations
cards.front: How does `deleteOne(filter)` differ from `deleteMany(filter)` in terms of the number of documents removed?
cards.back:
- `deleteMany(filter)` deletes every matching document. An empty filter (`{}`) deletes all documents without dropping the collection."

`deleteOne()` deletes at most one document; `deleteMany()` deletes all matching documents.
cards.key_takeaway: Use deleteOne to remove a single matching document and deleteMany to remove all matching documents.
cards.mermaid_diagram:
```mermaid
graph LR
    D["Deletion Cardinality"] --> A["deleteOne: Deletes first matching document"]
    D["Deletion Cardinality"] --> B["deleteMany: Deletes every matching document"]
```
cards.MindmapPath: VVIT MongoDB > 7. Document Deletion & Collection Pruning (CRUD Delete)
